audit_metadata.task: Task 29 — SIH26162 + AWS SHIP IT Compliance & Readiness Audit

detection.evidence: FIRMS CSV ingestion and spatio-temporal clustering implemented in scripts/cluster_firms_events.py over 5.19M detections; real-time automated streaming ingestion is not implemented.

industrial_association.evidence: OSM industrial extraction (extract_osm_industrial.py) and spatial joins (correlate_firms_osm.py) feed Dimension C (20% weight) based on containment, proximity, and distance decay.

persistence.evidence: Dimension B (25% weight) normalizes distinct detection days and detection count; successfully distinguishes chronic heat sources from transient events.

industrial_fire_vs_persistent_source.evidence: No validated ground-truth labels exist to distinguish accidental industrial fires from routine flares/kilns. Heuristic stratum models in Phase VIII cannot make this distinction.

satellite_evidence.evidence: Sentinel-2 STAC extraction (enrich_satellite_features.py) feeds Dimension E (15% weight) with SWIR contrast, NDVI, BSI, clear fraction, and temporal decay.

supervised_ml.type: Surrogate baselines only; no production model

safe_claims: Detects and clusters satellite-observed thermal anomalies into spatio-temporal events
Quantifies chronic thermal persistence up to 365-day observation windows
Measures spatial association and distance to OpenStreetMap industrial infrastructure
Incorporates contemporary Sentinel-2 SWIR/optical surface reflectance contrast
Calculates a deterministic, transparent evidence-weighted investigation priority score (0-100)
Computes an independent Evidence Confidence score (0-100)
Provides complete mathematical traceability and rank-ordered driver explanations
Correctly handles missing and stale satellite observations without safety assumptions
prohibited_claims: Detects industrial fires (cannot distinguish flares from accidental structure fires)
Classifies fires or predicts fire probability
Claims classification accuracy, precision, recall, or ROC-AUC metrics
Claims false-positive or false-negative rates against ground reality
Interprets low risk scores as proof of real-world safety

government_usefulness.justification: Provides prioritized, fully traceable, evidence-weighted guidance with explicit investigation actions for analysts reviewing complex thermal clusters.

aws_recommended_architecture.frontend: AWS Amplify Hosting (Single-page app with interactive India map and event inspector)
aws_recommended_architecture.compute: AWS Lambda (Stateless Python 3.11 container/layer running risk_engine)
aws_recommended_architecture.data_store: Amazon DynamoDB (ThermalTraceEvents table for instant event and explanation retrieval)
aws_recommended_architecture.object_storage: Amazon S3 (Hosting parquet datasets, geojson layers, and audit reports)
aws_recommended_architecture.event_bus: Amazon EventBridge (Scheduled ingestion and event-driven pipeline triggers)
aws_recommended_architecture.analyst_assistant: Amazon Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Sonnet grounded strictly on deterministic Task 28 JSON)

blockers: No web frontend exists for demonstration or analyst interaction
No AWS infrastructure is deployed and no public URL exists (mandatory for Ship It)
No ground-truth human labels exist to enable legitimate supervised fire classification
next_steps: Step 1: Build a modern, premium Single-Page Application frontend (React/HTML5/MapLibre) displaying the 100 pilot events, risk scores, and Task 28 explanations.
Step 2: Package risk_engine and Task 28 explainability into a lightweight AWS Lambda handler.
Step 3: Deploy data to Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3 for sub-100ms querying.
Step 4: Expose endpoints via Amazon API Gateway (/events, /events/{id}, /score).
Step 5: Deploy the frontend to AWS Amplify Hosting to establish a live public URL.
Step 6: Add Amazon Bedrock integration strictly for generating grounded natural-language intelligence memos from Task 28 JSON.
Step 7: Conduct Phase VI human ground-truth labeling to unlock legitimate supervised ML in future phases.
